newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan, Israel discuss lifting obstacles to trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan, Israel discuss lifting obstacles to trade.

text.p: Jordanian Trade Minister Hani al-Mulqi met his Israeli opposite number Natan Sharansky in Amman on Sunday to try to lift obstacles to trade between the two countries.

Mulqi told reporters they discussed procedures for border crossings and Israeli specification requirements, areas which Jordanian businessmen say are hindering sales both to Israel and Palestinian markets in the West Bank.

"Today we discussed the measures which we can follow to ease the obstacles on the bridge to trade between the two sides. We hope that traders in Jordan will notice a clear improvement in this operation during the summer," Mulqi said.
Sharansky said some of the obstacles could be lifted soon, but did not elaborate.

"We both agree our economic cooperation has unique potential and those problems which surround our way can be removed very quickly. It's a question not of years or months, some of them can be removed in weeks," he said.

But Sharansky defended tight security measures at Israel's borders and on the Israeli-controlled crossing between Jordan and the West Bank, which Jordanian exporters have criticised as excessive and causing unnecessary delays.
"When there are...explosions in the centre of Jerusalem and Tel Aviv and dozens of people are killed it is something you have to take very seriously into account," he said.

The two countries, which signed a peace deal in 1994, opened their borders to trade for the first time in June last year. Figures for the first six months of trade showed that Israel exported goods to Jordan worth $12.25 million compared to $5.75 million worth of trade going the other way.

Earlier on Sunday Sharansky toured a industrial park in Jordan's northern city of Irbid, where a number of Israeli firms have set up joint ventures, mainly in textile industries in Jordan, taking advantage of cheaper labour costs.
Mulqi said Israel's free-trade agreement with the United States meant that the Jordanian-made products could have access to U.S. markets too.

"In the field of joint investment there is a possibility for Jordanian goods to enter the American markets under the principle of free trade which Israel enjoys with the United States, we hope that this will allow the (industrial zone) in Irbid to enjoy the privilege of free trade wih United States."
